product.name: PAINT RUSH - executive demo of on-site paint mixing cost
product.description: An 8-bit, Game Boy-style browser demo showing that while staff mix tins to order, the shop floor is empty and walk-ins leave without buying; then the same day replayed with large orders sent to a central hub.
product.note: The backlog when tracker.kind is local or none. Plan: docs/plan-paint-rush.md. Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md.

scaffold.title: Project scaffold with a Game Boy canvas and an offline single-file build
scaffold.description: Set up the project so every later ticket has gates, a screen and a build. Vite + TypeScript, run with Bun. A 160x144 canvas scaled by whole-pixel factors and centred (letterboxed), drawn only in the four Game Boy greens defined once in src/styles/tokens.css. A placeholder title screen reading PAINT RUSH and PRESS SPACE. `bun run build` emits one self-contained HTML file (all JS, CSS and assets inlined) that runs from file:// with no network, for presenting from a laptop.
acceptance_criteria: package.json has dev, build, test, typecheck, lint and check scripts; `bun run check` runs typecheck, lint and tests and passes
src/styles/tokens.css defines the four palette colours; no other file under src/ holds a raw colour literal (check ui passes)
The canvas keeps a 160x144 logical resolution, scales by an integer factor, uses nearest-neighbour rendering, and stays fully visible at phone and desktop viewports
`bun run build` produces dist/paint-rush.html; opening it via file:// with networking disabled shows the title screen (a Playwright test asserts this)
.forger/ui.json paths, tokens, start and url match the real project, and `screenshot` writes docs/screenshots/index-*.png
Playwright and axe-core are dev dependencies; `check a11y` passes on the title screen
README.md says what the demo is and how to run, build and present it
reuse: vite-plugin-singlefile (or equivalent) for the inlined build
docs/design/two-run-results wireframe for the title screen content

sim-engine.title: Deterministic shop simulation for the today and hub scenarios
sim-engine.description: The model behind the demo, pure and tested, with no rendering. An event-driven simulation in shop minutes over one shift, driven by a seeded RNG and a parameter object (defaults in GLOSSARY.md and docs/plan-paint-rush.md). Walk-ins arrive at a Poisson rate; a free staff member serves them for the service time and they spend the average sale; otherwise they wait and leave as a lost sale at the patience limit. Mix orders arrive at their own rate with a tin count from the order-size mix and tin sizes priced per size; a free staff member takes the order and is off the floor for minutes-per-tin x tins. Scenario `today` mixes everything in store; scenario `hub` sends large orders (over the hub threshold) to the central hub, which records a 2h delivery and never occupies staff. Both scenarios share one seed so arrivals are identical (ADR 0001). Output: per-scenario metrics and an ordered event timeline the renderer can replay.
acceptance_criteria: Same seed and parameters give an identical timeline and metrics; different seeds differ
The today and hub runs for one seed have identical walk-in and mix-order arrival times and tin counts
In hub, no order above the hub threshold is mixed in store; each appears as a hub dispatch with a delivery time 120 shop minutes later
A walk-in who waits past the patience limit is recorded as a lost sale worth the average sale; one served in time is not
With one staff member mixing, a walk-in arriving during the mix finds nobody free (floor empty)
Metrics include tins mixed in store, orders sent to hub, walk-ins served, walk-ins lost, sales lost GBP and staff minutes off the floor
`bun run sim --json [--seed n]` prints both scenarios' metrics as JSON; a test runs it
Engine code imports nothing from the DOM or the renderer
reuse: GLOSSARY.md terms for type and field names

shop-scene.title: Animated shop scene that replays one scenario
shop-scene.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/shop-scene/ (set status to not_started to release). Replays one scenario's timeline on the Game Boy canvas at the time scale (default 1 real second = 5 shop minutes, ADR 0002) with original pixel art only: a top-down shop floor with door, aisles and counter; a mixing room behind a wall; staff walking between them; walk-ins queueing with a wait meter, an '!' bubble and walking out with a '-GBP95' pop; a tin progress bar ('TIN 3/8'); a status bar with scenario name, shop clock, served and lost counters and GBP lost; a Pokemon-style text box with narration beats. In hub, a van leaves the loading bay with '2H DELIVERY' for each large order.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered counters at the end of a replay equal the sim-engine metrics for the same seed
Replay length equals shift length / time scale (8h at 1 s = 5 min plays in 96 s), within one frame
The floor is drawn empty whenever the timeline says no staff member is on it
All sprites and tiles are original and drawn in the four token colours; no third-party game assets
The UI states in the wireframe (opening, overflow queue, no-canvas fallback) are implemented
docs/screenshots/ is updated by `screenshot`, and docs/design/shop-scene/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

two-run-results.title: Presentation flow: today, results, with hub, comparison
two-run-results.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/two-run-results/. The full pitch on SPACE: title -> today replay -> today results -> hub replay (same seed) -> comparison. Comparison shows today vs hub for walk-ins lost and sales lost, then sales saved per day, per week, per year and across N stores, with the footnote 'Excludes central prep and delivery costs.' R reshuffles the day (new seed) and replays. Results are mirrored into a visually hidden live region.
acceptance_criteria: SPACE advances through every step in order; at the comparison it replays the same day, R starts a new seed
Comparison figures equal the sim-engine metrics; week, year and store extrapolations use the parameters for trading days and stores
The excludes-costs footnote is always shown on the comparison
Large GBP values are shortened to fit the text box (e.g. GBP1.2M) and a zero-loss day reads 'No sales lost today'
The live region contains the comparison as text, and `check a11y` passes on every step
docs/screenshots/ is updated and docs/design/two-run-results/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

settings.title: Settings menu to edit every demo parameter
settings.description: Waits for the owner to approve the wireframe at docs/design/settings/. A Game Boy-style menu opened with S from the title, keyboard only: shift hours, time scale, staff on floor (1-4), walk-ins per hour, mix orders per hour, service time, patience, average sale, minutes per tin, order-size mix, tin prices per size, hub threshold, stores, trading days per year. Reshuffle and reset-to-defaults actions. Values persist in browser storage and feed the next run.
acceptance_criteria: Every parameter in src/sim/params.ts is editable from the menu and the next run uses the edited value
Order-size percentages that do not total 100 show 'MUST TOTAL 100' and block BACK
Values survive a reload; with storage unavailable they still apply for the session and a note says so
Reset restores the documented defaults
The menu is fully keyboard operable and `check a11y` passes
docs/screenshots/ is updated and docs/design/settings/ is moved into docs/progress/ per the archive rule

take-control.title: Take-control mode for the presenter
take-control.description: An optional mode, toggled with C during a replay, where the presenter decides what a free staff member does next when a walk-in and a mix order are both waiting. Autoplay stays the default. The simulation must expose a decision hook so the same engine serves both modes deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: With no input the mode behaves exactly like autoplay
A choice changes the outcome and the metrics reflect it
The engine accepts a decision policy; autoplay is the default policy and is covered by the existing tests
The on-screen prompt says which keys choose what
reuse: shop-scene text box for the prompt

chiptune-sound.title: Chiptune sound effects, muted by default
chiptune-sound.description: Original square-wave effects generated with the Web Audio API for walk-in, walkout, tin done and van leaving. Muted on load; M toggles and the status bar shows the state. No audio files.
acceptance_criteria: No sound plays until M is pressed
Each named event triggers its effect when unmuted
No audio file is added; effects are synthesised
The built single file still runs offline
